explanation:
Neurons are structurally polarized, meaning they have a specific direction for signal flow. Dendrons (also known as dendrites) are the branching extensions of the cell body that receive incoming signals from other neurons or sensory receptors and conduct these impulses towards the cell body (soma). In contrast, axons conduct impulses away from the cell body, while the myelin sheath serves as an insulator to speed up conduction, and synaptic nodes are gaps in the myelin sheath where saltatory conduction occurs.
